speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We will continue to monitor the progress and explore additional measures as needed.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: With regard to the Member's question on renewable energy in buildings, the most promising option is the solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on the rooftop.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: There is already good take-up of such PVs today because the costs have come down.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The BCA Green Mark Scheme also encourages this by recognising projects that have solar panels on their roofs or have conducted a solar feasibility study.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: However, there are physical constraints for some buildings that limit the adoption of solar energy.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We will continue to explore how to increase the use of solar and other renewable options in our buildings.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One is in relation to part (c) of my question, whether there are plans to make the BCA Green Mark Scheme compulsory.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second question is with regard to energy efficiency.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We have been discussing about single-use plastic bags but, in addition, the usage of energy in an efficient way in buildings is actually a very important factor.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Does the Ministry of National Development (MND) have plans to ensure that companies and buildings use, for example, more efficient air-conditioners, and efficient usage of them in terms of setting temperature levels?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My third supplementary question is: can MND share how they incorporate on an ongoing basis, progressively over the years, increasingly advanced sustainability elements and requirements in its assessment criteria?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We are still about 11 years or 12 more years away, including 2019.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: There are new sustainability measures probably that may emerge over time.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister of State share with us?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I just want to assure the Member that, certainly, we continuously look at how we put up the criteria for the Green Mark Scheme.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, the Green Mark awards or criteria do not only cover energy per se.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Energy efficiency is just one aspect, that is, the air-cons or chillers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But it also includes ventilation, lightings, escalators, lifts and how we do system monitoring over these systems.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: At the same time, we also look at water efficiency, sustainable operations in management, even the indoor environment quality and other green features as well.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, that includes whether you have green rooftops and so forth.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, these are elements which we consider today.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Of course, the status will change over time and we will review.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, that is one way in terms of industry push.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, you find, for example, Bugis Junction Towers and Bugis Junction, and the 85-year-old Police building, these are old buildings that have been retrofitted and today have achieved not just the Green Mark status but the Green Mark Platinum status as well.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, it is possible for really old buildings to be retrofitted.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We are seeing some movement there, largely also because some of the technologies are more established, and you also find the industry a lot more able to cater and to provide for more green technologies or green sustainability elements to be put into our buildings.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But, of course, for existing buildings, it is a bit more difficult.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But today, they also score points for keeping the air-conditions to 23 to 25 degrees Celsius, and having efficient systems.
